description: Needs an Alion account or an x402 payment (not free on this open address). Before a person applies, shares a passport or answers a recruiter: is the company real, any signs of a job scam, can it sponsor the person's visa, is it worth applying. Our own rules over public data, not a model: company registers and legal entities, the domain's age (RDAP), the website and its certificate, mail protection (SPF, DMARC), lookalike domains, OFAC and EU sanctions, the company's own hiring board against its postings, scam patterns in up to 80 of its job adverts (requests for money or documents, messenger-only contact...), the UK, US, Canadian, Dutch, Irish, Danish and Australian visa registers against the person's citizenship, ghost and reposted roles, pay and time to fill. Answers a verdict (ok, warning, risk), the four answers, every section's facts and points with their sources, and the advice before an apply. Pass message with a recruiter's email or chat text to check whether it really comes from this company (sender domain, links, scam signs). For an assistant a person connected to their own Alion account (OAuth or an API key): 5 credits from that account, the report is reused free for 30 days and opens on the site too, a high-risk verdict costs nothing; a message check is free with the report. An observation on the date, not a guarantee. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

company.description: The employer: its web domain ("acme.com"), Alion id, exact name or any url on its site.

job.description: Optional: the job the person looks at - an Alion job id or an alion.io/job/... link (sets the company when company is left out).

message.description: Optional: a recruiter's email or chat message (20-8000 characters, with the sender's address when there is one) to check against the company.

refresh.description: Build the report again although one from the last 30 days exists (charged again).
